id: Stable slug: race type + state + district/seat. Use as the key on the site.
race_type: Senate | Governor | House | Attorney General | Secretary of State | Judicial | State Legislature (Upper) | State Legislature (Lower) | Ballot Measure
district: House district number, legislative district, 'special', or measure name; null for statewide offices.
active: false = decided earlier in 2026 or not on the November ballot; exclude from rankings.
candidates: [{party, name}] as listed in the workbook (may include short annotations). party NP = nonpartisan (Nebraska legislature).
rating: Cook rating where available (House: derived band — see Provenance).
margin: Projected margin in points (null when unopposed). Candidate races: D (or the leading non-R challenger) minus R. Ballot measures: yes minus no.
display_name: Short label for the race, e.g. 'Maine Senate', 'OH-10', 'Alabama House District 3'.
margin_source: Where the margin comes from (F1 average, poll median, PVI baseline, past result + environment, ...).
sigma: Uncertainty (t-distribution scale, points) used for this race.
win_probability: Senate/Governor only: {candidate, party, opponent, p} = chance the named candidate finishes ahead.
turnout_base: Electorate size used in the turnout term (statewide 2020 turnout; district turnout for state legislature).
voter_power: 0–100 within race type (not comparable across race types). 0 = unopposed or decided. State legislature: scaled within each state, both chambers pooled (the best seat in a state = 100), so it is not comparable across states; use detail.voter_power_national for the all-states score.
unopposed: No opponent on the November ballot.
donation: Senate/House only: {per_dollar_power 0–100 within race type, fec_receipts (USD, nominees, cycle to date), fec_reports_through, independent_expenditures (USD, nominees, support + oppose counted equally), money_used (fec_receipts + independent_expenditures, the money behind per_dollar_power)}.
caveats: Data-quality flags to show on the race page (thin polling, missing FEC reports, 3-way race, ...).
last_verified: Date the row was last checked.
detail: Race-type-specific extras. State legislature: committee_targets (DLCC/RSLC target-list labels, text), chamber_tier, chamber_p_dem_majority (simulated chance Democrats win the chamber, 0-1, static), seat_pivotal_prob (simulated chance this seat decides control, 0-1, static; null where the chamber is not modeled). From v50 also: voter_power_national (state legislature, all-states 0-100 score) and sabato_close_chamber (true if Sabato's Crystal Ball lists the chamber as within a few seats of flipping; list supplied by the project owner 2026-10-22).
flip: public/data/flip/state_flip_summary.json (states ranked by chance a legislative chamber flips; sabato_focus lists the Sabato-flagged states first) and flip/states/<slug>.json (chambers, top seats, ballot measures, other races). Probabilities assume the workbook's national environment of D+12.5; p_flip_by_national_env gives D+4.5, D+8.5 and D+12.5. p_flip is null where a chamber is not modeled or is a bipartisan coalition (Alaska).
